messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] SEV2 - LATAM-West1 egress failures detected. Error rate spike (502/504) across multiple edge POPs. Auto-pager triggered.

maya: paging oncall, taking this in. jumping into the thread now — tagging @sam and @elena for network/infra. any immediate customer red lines? :rotating_light:

sam: seeing elevated 5xx for latam-west1 on gateway-proxy. tcp retrans and some RSTs. provider-side peering looks noisy based on initial traces.

elena: confirmed failures from our health-checks to 10.12.0.0/16 egress ranges. BGP flaps showing on the carrier side. Affected: CL/PE/AR prefixes, roughly ~8% traffic.

maya: plan: 1) divert egress for latam-west1 to latam-east1/eu-west1; 2) update status page + public comms; 3) notify CS for impacted enterprise customers; 4) keep mitigation until carrier stabilizes.

nora: customer-impact summary: 7 customers >1% error, 2 enterprise Dedicated tenants (C-1192, C-2034) should get immediate notice. drafting targeted message now.

sam: running reroute playbook (will post command output).

```
# ops: divert egress
./ops/reroute --region latam-west1 --to latam-east1,eu-west1 --type egress --confirm
```

sam: applied the reroute. routes propagated to edge proxies. initial metrics: ~70% of flows moved within 90s; remainder are sticky TCP sessions. watching KV cache and session drains.

elena: note: some long-lived websocket connections will require client reconnects; adding header-based TTL to encourage reconnects where safe.

maya: suggested short status page copy (for ops to paste):
"We are investigating increased errors and timeouts for requests served from latam-west1. We are diverting outbound traffic while we work with our network provider. Some customers may see elevated 5xx errors; we are mitigating by routing traffic to latam-east1 and eu-west1. Updates every 15 minutes."

nora: CS message drafted and queued for sending to affected customers. enterprise notif includes workaround: configure multi-region fallback (if supported) and contact for dedicated SLAs.

pagerduty: @maya acknowledged the page. ETA for full traffic migration estimated 30-45m.

maya: quick runbook excerpt for oncall handoff / executed steps:
- action: divert egress (sam) — DONE
- action: confirm customer list & notify (nora) — IN PROGRESS
- action: escalate to network provider and request BGP logs (elena) — IN PROGRESS
- action: post status & schedule follow-ups (maya) — IN PROGRESS

elena: provider update: they reported a partial peering outage affecting latam-west1 exchanges; provider working on internal reroutes. estimated time to stable ~45m (subject to change).

maya: publishing status page and cross-posting to #customers-ops. Full status copy below (will also push to status.redwood.ai):
---
We are currently diverting outbound traffic from latam-west1 due to an upstream peering issue causing increased 5xx errors. Traffic is being routed to latam-east1 and eu-west1 where capacity permits. Some customers may experience increased latency or transient errors; dedicated tenants may see partial impact. Engineers are coordinating with the network provider. We expect mitigation within ~45 minutes; updates every 15 minutes.
---

sam: perf notes: token-level median latency +120ms during failover, tail P99 increased briefly but trending down. Autoscale triggered extra workers in latam-east1 to absorb redirected load.

elena: opened ticket with provider and requested BGP dump + timeline. logging link for internal reference: https://internal.logs/redwood/2030123456

nora: sent targeted enterprise notificiations. included status link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2030123456 and recommended temporary throttles for ingest-heavy customers.

maya: handoff plan: @sam remain primary for next 30m for routing & mitigation, then hand to @elena for provider liaison and postmortem. @nora continue CS comms and collect customer reports. moving to incident-postmortem channel once stable :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident SEV2 latam-west1: status -> Mitigating. Next automated update in 15m.
